page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-4 is a compute-focused x86_64 virtual machine instance belonging to the N1 server family. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs based on 2 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.3 GHz with 2 threads per core. The instance is provisioned with 4.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high compute-to-memory ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU. Cache configuration includes 32 KB L1d cache, 0.25 MB L2 cache, and 45 MB shared L3 cache. It lacks dedicated local storage and includes no GPU hardware accelerators.

In synthetic benchmarks, the n1-highcpu-4 exhibits lower performance tiers relative to modern cloud infrastructure. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 926.0 and a multi-core score of 1979.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 3374.03. Memory bandwidth testing shows 25.58 GB/sec uncached read throughput and 21.69 GB/sec uncached write throughput. Application-level metrics reflect 2.8 million SET operations per second in Redis and a static web serving throughput of 2.92 GB/sec. Small language model prompt processing achieves 160.16 tokens per second on a 135M parameter model.

The resource profile highlights a low-memory, entry-level dedicated vCPU configuration. Given its legacy processor architecture and lower resource density, the instance provides steady execution but exhibits limited multi-threaded throughput compared to newer generations. This instance type is suited for light compile tasks, basic web serving, utility scripts, batch processing, and non-memory-intensive CI/CD pipelines where dedicated CPU allocation is required without requiring high RAM capacity.
description: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-4 is an entry-tier x86_64 compute-optimized server equipped with 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical Intel Xeon cores at 2.3 GHz and 4.0 GB of RAM. Lacking bundled local storage and GPU accelerators, it provides a 1:1 vCPU-to-RAM ratio tailored for memory-light execution. Benchmark results place its compute and memory capabilities in lower performance brackets, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 1979.0, a PassMark CPU score of 3374.03, and uncached memory read bandwidth of 25.58 GB/sec. Operational throughput reaches 2.8 million Redis SET operations per second and 2.92 GB/sec for static web serving. While offering dedicated core allocation without credit-based throttling, its legacy architecture limits high-throughput scaling. The instance is best matched for lightweight CI/CD tasks, simple batch jobs, basic web serving, and utility processing workloads that demand continuous CPU access with low memory overhead.
